newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN chief speaks to Sahnoun, more rebel talks seen.
newsitem.headline: UN chief speaks to Sahnoun, more rebel talks seen.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Saturday spoke to his special envoy in Central Africa who is expected to meet rebel leaders again in an attempt to work out a ceasefire in Zaire.

U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said Mohamed Sahnoun, who went to the rebel-held eastern Zaire border town of Goma for talks with rebel leader Laurent Kabila, was "trying to work out modalities for a ceasefire and talks."

Sahnoun, appointed chief mediator by the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity (OAU), went to Goma on Saturday from the Rwandan capital Kigali where he held talks with President Pasteur Bizimungu and Vice-President Maj-Gen. Paul Kagame on the fighting in Zaire.

Diplomats in New York said they did not believe Kabila's supporters wanted the fighting to move further to the West now that they had captured Kisangani, Zaire's third largest city. But at the same time they did not see immediate signs of successful negotiations, despite earlier optimism.
In Zaire, a regional military source said on Saturday the rebels were advancing on the town of Pweto on Lake Tanganyika in the mineral-rich Shaba province.
Both the United States and Britain have in the last few days urged Kabila's allies in Rwanda and Uganda to use their influence with Kabila to persuade him to stop fighting.
So far Kabila has accepted a U.N. peace plan as a basis for talks but rejected its call for a ceasefire before talks with the Zairean government.
The rebels say they want to overthrow Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko, who had surgery for prostate cancer last August and is now resting in France.

Sahnoun also saw Kabila on Thursday in northern Uganda at talks chaired by Ugandan President and regional power broker Yoweri Museveni. Diplomats in the Ugandan capital Kampala said Museveni, accused by Zaire of backing Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, did not take sides in the dispute at the meeting.

France has wanted to organise an intervention force but other European nations as well as the United States are cool to the idea. Annan has also championed a force to protect Rwandan refugees caught in the fighting in eastern Zaire and without access to relief aid.
He now is advocating monitors or peacekeepers to verify any ceasefire that may be negotiated as well as help the refugees return home.
